gen-gf-noto-serif-oriya-fs-epilogue: Epilogue draws curvy, wire-thin monoline letters with stubby ascender tips. Noto Serif Oriya does its best work in mellow thick-thin strokes and a bookish tone, while the plain sans simply glides along, unshaded and tall-bodied.
gen-gf-noto-serif-oriya-fs-public-sans: Noto Serif Oriya sets a literary tone, its crossbars a touch finer than the main stems and its contrast tempered. And Public Sans follows with a hefty sans lowercase and broad, open curves that ground the heading.
gen-gf-noto-serif-oriya-fs-supreme: Strokes that thicken and thin in small, gentle steps give Noto Serif Oriya its bookish voice. Supreme holds a heavy, crisp band of sans-serif text beneath it, its letters kept open rather than curled shut.
gen-gf-noto-serif-oriya-general-sans: Noto Serif Oriya has a literary lean. It excels at middle-of-the-road contrast with compact extenders, while General Sans shines at smooth, unthinned curves and a plain sans x-height that fills the line.
gen-gf-noto-serif-oriya-manrope: Slight but clear stroke modulation gives Noto Serif Oriya a literary, bookish feel that never jolts or flattens the eye. Manrope's single constant line keeps that sans body bright.
gen-gf-noto-serif-oriya-montserrat: Noto Serif Oriya brings a calm thick-thin rhythm and tall lowercase bodies, giving its literary headings a bookish, tempered feel. Montserrat glides beneath, a constant-width sans-serif line with generous counters.
gen-gf-noto-serif-oriya-satoshi: Bookish yet bright, with literary strokes carrying a mild pen-like variation up top. And Satoshi's soaring x-height and open e, cut in one width like a bent paperclip, make the sans below feel unsqueezed.
gen-gf-noto-serif-oriya-switzer: A gradual weight change, never an abrupt snap, gives Noto Serif Oriya its literary, bookish pull. And Switzer's tubular, wire-like sans-serif letters, with tall waist lines and wide-open c tips, would keep a longer passage moving smoothly.
gen-gf-noto-serif-oriya-work-sans: Literary in mood, Noto Serif Oriya shows modest stress in its curves and compact extenders. But if the heading is made small, Work Sans, a sans-serif with high mean lines and skimming, steady strokes, would likely overpower it.
gen-gf-noto-serif-ottoman-siyaq-archivo: Tall lowercase, mild stress, editorial polish. Noto Serif Ottoman Siyaq leads in a literary voice, and Archivo, a plain sans with outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height, would carry a long page with steady confidence.
